// diagnostic

E3114

`{subject}` carries a caller-chosen address to `{operation}`

What

`{subject}` carries a caller-chosen address to `{operation}`

Why

Code outside the kernel files reaches `{subject}` without a gate, so the address `{operation}` uses would skip the kernel's audit.

Fix

Take an owner or a `View<T>` instead of the address, make the field `priv`, or mark the function `#Unsafe("…")` so each caller vouches for the address.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E3114: tests/ui/E3113_runtime_unit_source_outside_kernel/stderr.

Error [jet.RawMemoryOutsideKernel]: `os_load_i64` at Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Host.jet:3 is a raw memory operation outside the package's memory kernel
  --> tests/ui/E3113_runtime_unit_source_outside_kernel/run.jet:16:65
    |
 16 |     #Unsafe("the host holds the word at this address") { return os_load_i64(address) }
    |                                                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Raw memory operations stand only in the kernel files `policy.memory` names, so the package's memory safety is audited in one place.
 Fix: Outside the kernel, read and write through a `[T]` list or a `View<T>` a kernel owner hands out; to make `Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Host.jet` a kernel file, add `Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Host.jet` to `policy.memory` in `package.jet`.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3113

Error [jet.RawAddressIntoKernel]: `_word` carries the caller-chosen address `address` to `os_load_i64`
  --> tests/ui/E3113_runtime_unit_source_outside_kernel/run.jet:10:77
    |
 10 |     #Unsafe("the kernel's own leaf reads a word its caller lends") { return os_load_i64(address) }
    |                                                                             ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Code outside the kernel files calls `_word` without a gate, so the address `os_load_i64` uses would skip the kernel's audit.
 Fix: Take an owner or a `View<T>` in place of `address`, or mark `_word` `#Unsafe("…")` so each caller vouches for the address.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3114
